blocks.text: Plant and synthetic evidence comes from the original study and EFSA. The existence of a microbial-source EU specification amendment is confirmed by the retrieved 2022/672 record, but its full annex was not recovered and is not reproduced as a complete specification.[41][20][18]

**A public plant-process example—100 g dried knotweed root, not an industrial SOP.** Wang, Liu and Chen used approximately 40-mesh root powder, soaked 100 g with 95% ethanol at 1:6 g/mL for about 12 hours, then refluxed at about 80°C three times for one hour each. Combined extract was rotary-evaporated under vacuum at 65°C.[41] Dry-extract yield was 13.3% of starting powder, while resveratrol was 3.3% of that extract. These different denominators must remain explicit.[41]

The dried extract was milled, mixed with water at 1:30 g/mL, treated in an ultrasonic bath at 50°C for 20 minutes and filtered. The aqueous phase was adjusted with hydrochloric acid to pH 1 and reflux-hydrolyzed at 75°C for 8 hours.[41] Polydatin conversion contributed newly formed free resveratrol. The approximately fourfold increase reported by the authors is not 400% recovery of the initial free compound.[41] Follow precursor disappearance, product formation and unknown/degradation peaks together.

The study used repeated equal-volume liquid–liquid extraction and washed the organic phase with alkaline aqueous solution at pH 8–9, exemplified by 5% sodium bicarbonate, approximately twice at equal phase volumes.[41] The final product contained over 73.8% resveratrol—not a commercial high-purity trans grade. Subsequent preparative-HPLC isolation for MS/NMR identity confirmation does not establish that purity for the entire final batch.[41]

The authors compared direct aqueous dilution of concentrated ethanol extract with drying and redispersion. The former removed some low-polarity compounds less effectively; they proposed that the latter promoted aggregation that could be filtered, while noting incomplete supporting figures.[41] Filtration therefore depends on upstream solvent/particle history as well as pore size. An energy-saving alternative that omits drying must demonstrate impurity removal and recovery equivalence.

For comparison, EFSA’s assessed synthetic product used a Wittig reaction, a trimethoxy intermediate and demethylation involving aluminium chloride and diisopropylamine, followed by isopropanol/water crystallization and ethanol/water recrystallization.[20] This creates a different impurity brief from knotweed. Public descriptions do not provide a complete batch-scale synthesis recipe.[20]

blocks.text: These are engineering recommendations. The original work used flasks, an ultrasonic bath, a rotary evaporator and separating funnels, not validated continuous production equipment.[41] Scale-up requires heat-transfer, corrosion, contacting, settling and solvent-safety assessment, not multiplication of laboratory minutes by batch mass.

**Documented failure 1—acid identity matters.** The knotweed authors initially used sulfuric acid at pH 1 and reported susceptibility of resveratrol and polydatin to oxidation under those conditions, then selected hydrochloric-acid reflux hydrolysis at the same pH.[41] This does not establish universal sulfuric-acid failure, but it invalidates an assumption that acids are interchangeable at equal pH. Investigate acid identity, contaminants, oxygen, metal contact and residence.

**Documented failure 2—analytical signal can conceal degradation.** Zupančič et al. found relative stability in acidic conditions and increasing degradation above pH 6.8 in their experiments. UV/VIS gave falsely high trans-resveratrol concentrations under unstable alkaline, light and elevated-temperature conditions; HPLC and UPLC specificity was confirmed.[30] Only the abstract was retrieved, without complete batch volume/concentration/time details, so pH 6.8 is a study observation, not a universal formulation prohibition. Long dissolution and cell assays need actual trans exposure measurements.

en.heading: Applications: physical form first

blocks.text: Purity and aqueous usability are independent. The 2015 study specifically examines how solubility/stability affect delivery research; apparent solubility changes must not be mistaken for stable target concentration.[30] Select the intended format—capsule/tablet, suspension/emulsion, clear drink or topical preparation—before buying crystals, micronized powder or a carrier grade.

blocks.text: These are proposed development tests. Loading, encapsulation efficiency, trans mass per serving and free fraction need separate definitions. A “10%” label can describe different quantities. Supplier methods and composition should precede brand claims. Auxiliary antioxidants or light-protective packaging do not eliminate the need for chemical stability measurement.[30]

A proposed matrix uses the same ingredient lot, a carrier candidate and carrier blank under final pH/packaging, with dark/light and routine/accelerated conditions. Follow total material, trans-specific assay, degradants and physical state. Falling supernatant with unchanged total suggests precipitation/adsorption; falling total trans prompts degradation/isomerization investigation. The corrective actions differ.

en.heading: Quality and regulation

blocks.text: Historical EU Decision 2016/1190 authorized its specified trans-resveratrol in adult capsule/tablet supplements at up to 150 mg/day with labeling conditions. Its then-annex included ≥99% trans, ≤0.5% total related substances and ≤0.1% any single related substance.[19] These illustrate the combined identity/use/impurity framework, not all sources, food formats or current 2026 specifications. Regulation 2022/672 subsequently amended microbial-source specifications; the current consolidated Union-list entry still needs complete confirmation.[18]

A concrete QA lesson appears in EFSA Table 2: three mercury results were reported as ≤1.0 mg/kg against a ≤0.1 mg/kg specification, and the opinion noted noncompliance with that specification.[20] Do not reinterpret this as measured mercury of exactly 1 mg/kg in each batch. The reporting threshold cannot demonstrate compliance with the lower limit; a sufficiently sensitive retest is needed. Supplier analytical/reporting limits must support the acceptance decision.

Use chromatography capable of resolving isomers and relevant impurities, rather than nonspecific UV absorbance under unstable conditions.[30] For knotweed, track polydatin, emodin, other anthraquinones and unknowns through clearance; the original study used C18 chromatography, external standard quantitation and MS/NMR identity confirmation.[41] Synthetic routes need a process-specific related-compound/reagent list; EFSA’s diisopropylamine and related-substance controls are specific to its evaluated process, not universal to all sources.[20]

Certificates should specify dry/as-is basis, moisture, ash, solvents, carrier and active mass. A hypothetical 1 g formulated material containing 10% trans on the entire as-is preparation basis corresponds to 100 mg nominal input; that calculation fails if 10% means dry basis or encapsulation efficiency. This is a metrology example, not an intake recommendation. Molecular identity does not erase botanical part, extraction solvent, precursor hydrolysis or source impurities.

en.heading: Research significance and handover

blocks.text: The knotweed paper connects solubility, acidity and hydrolysis to measurable fractionation, while its approximately 73.8%-grade endpoint exposes the remaining gap to highly purified material.[41] The stability study reveals why analytical methods can misstate exposure in prolonged cell/dissolution experiments.[30] EFSA evaluates source, impurities, intake and toxicology as one defined material rather than inferring high-intake safety from natural occurrence.[20]
